purpose: Prove Dataverse MVP operational store readiness locally as CONTRACT evidence only: a read-only preflight contract describing the expected `pac auth who`, `pac env who`, and environment-settings evidence shape with every tenant value marked VERIFY IN TENANT and deferred-to-tenant; a story-scoped write policy mapping which manifest tables/columns each future implementation story needs (without forcing the full target shape upfront); and rollback/audit boundary statements per planned write scope. Write scripts stay disabled (writeScriptsDisabled=true) until Doug approves Dataverse sandbox writes and publisher prefix; those approvals are present as PENDING entries and no approval receipt is fabricated. No live pac/tenant call is performed in this slice; every would-be live write appears as a deferred entry naming its receipt gate.

preflightContract.matchPolicy: When the live preflight runs, the `pac env who` environment ID and organization ID MUST equal dataverse-mvp-schema-manifest.json target.environmentId and target.organizationId; a mismatch blocks every write. This slice records the expected SHAPE only and defers the concrete values to the tenant; no concrete environment or organization id is recorded here.

pendingApprovals.question: Are Dataverse sandbox writes allowed after read-only preflight proves the target environment?
pendingApprovals.receiptGate: No approval receipt (CR-LOCAL-*) is fabricated for this approval until Doug explicitly approves; dataverse-apply-mvp-schema.ps1 must stay in DRY RUN ONLY mode and writeScriptsDisabled stays true.

pendingApprovals.question: What Dataverse publisher prefix should confirm the placeholder prefix before any solution creation write?
pendingApprovals.receiptGate: No approval receipt (CR-LOCAL-*) is fabricated for this approval until Doug confirms the publisher prefix; publisher/solution creation writes stay disabled.

dryRunSchemaManifest.fullShapeDescription: dataverse-mvp-schema-manifest.json describes the full MVP target shape (14 tables, 15 global choices, model-driven app, sitemap). The dry run MAY reference the full shape for planning, but no implementation story is allowed to force all tables/columns to be created before that story needs them.

storyScopedWritePolicy.writeScopeNote: Story 1.1 only needs the Source Record table and its capture/boundary columns; it must not force Work Item or Receipt tables to exist.
Story 1.3 needs Work Item, Work Item Source, and Receipt tables with the proposed verb only; it must not force Graph or Memory tables to exist.
Story 1.5 needs the source_drifted verb on Receipt and the drift_evidence role on Receipt Source; it must not force Work Item state columns to change.
Story 2.1 needs the Work Item execution shell columns and the proposed-verb receipt chain; it must not force approval-scope columns to mutate.

Story 2.3 is the canonical receipt-backed mutation story; every live Dataverse mutation from earlier slices is gated to this story. It needs only the state-change columns and the receipt verbs it exercises.
Story 3.1 needs only the Brief table; it must not force Memory or Instruction tables to exist.
Story 4.1 needs only Graph Entity and Graph Edge tables; it must not force Memory or Instruction tables to exist.
Story 4.4 needs Memory Candidate, Approved Instruction, and Receipt tables with the memory_promoted verb; it must not force Skill or Minion tables to exist.

rollbackAuditBoundaries.rollbackBoundary: Roll back to the last append-only receipt boundary: every com_councilreceipt row is append-only (com_append_only_locked=true), so a failed state-change apply is rolled back by appending a corrective receipt rather than editing or deleting prior rows; the affected com_councilworkitem.com_state_group is restored to the before-state recorded on the failed receipt.
rollbackAuditBoundaries.auditBoundary: Every state-change write emits a manifest-verb com_councilreceipt with com_before_state, com_after_state, com_idempotency_key, and com_evidence_refs; the receipt is the audit row. No state change is auditably complete without a backing receipt.
rollbackAuditBoundaries.receiptGate: Live com_councilworkitem.com_state_group mutation is receipt-gated to Epic 2 Story 2.3; no live mutation is performed in this slice.

rollbackAuditBoundaries.rollbackBoundary: Roll back to the prior source version: a supersession is reversed by capturing a new superseding record that points com_parent_ref back at the pre-supersession record, never by editing the superseded record or its prior rationale; the superseded record and its receipts stay byte-identical.
rollbackAuditBoundaries.auditBoundary: Every drift/supersession write emits a source_drifted com_councilreceipt bound to its source evidence by a com_councilreceiptsource row with com_evidence_role=drift_evidence; the drift receipt is the audit row for the version transition.
rollbackAuditBoundaries.receiptGate: Live com_councilsourcerecord version/supersession mutation is receipt-gated to Epic 2 Story 2.3; no live mutation is performed in this slice.

rollbackAuditBoundaries.rollbackBoundary: Roll back the schema apply by deleting the CouncilOfMinionsMVP unmanaged solution in the sandbox environment; unmanaged solution deletion removes the Council tables/choices it introduced. The committed dataverse-mvp-schema-manifest.json is the re-apply source of truth, and the tenant decision packet records Doug's approval before any such apply runs.
rollbackAuditBoundaries.auditBoundary: The schema apply is gated behind a Doug-approved read-only preflight that proves target.environmentId and target.organizationId match `pac env who`; the preflight evidence and the tenant decision packet are the audit trail for the write authorization. The apply script's DRY RUN ONLY marker is the no-write boundary until approval.
rollbackAuditBoundaries.receiptGate: The schema apply itself is not a Council receipt event; it is a platform provisioning step approved through the tenant decision packet. It must stay in DRY RUN ONLY mode (writeScriptsDisabled=true) until Doug approves dataverseSandboxWrites and publisherPrefix.
